Some of the girls in this ward are restricted in making major or all decisions in life because of poverty
If she is a young married woman, she is unable to make most of the decisions because she must submit to her husband
A young woman does not have a choice if her parents can no longer afford her school fees, she cannot decide to continue with education if there is no money

YOUNG WOMEN
1. CONSERVATION AGRICULTURE – BASIN METHOD
As young women, this method is easy for us because we do not own cattle to practice other farming methods. I just need a hoe to dig the basins
The method saves money because fertilizer can be easily replaced by manure
It saves manure because we place it directly into the basin. I can use the same basin for some years in a row. This means that the manure in the basin keeps getting richer or maturing
The method ensures that I get a healthy crop
I can use dead leaves instead of manure or fertilizer
I prefer conservation agriculture because it conserves water and moisture in the field
One can easily plant 4 seeds in each basin which gives a high yield
The fact that we plant in straight lines provides ventilation to the crops
The mulching restrains the growth of weeds thus weeding is less
We are encouraged to plant early in conservation agriculture, meaning that the basins conserve water from the first drop and our crops grow fast
2. NEW IMPROVED SEED VARIETIES
Our area does not receive much rainfall that is why we opt for sorghum seeds such as the Marcia and Sila
I agree with her. That is also the reason why we go for maize varieties SC 403 and Pioneer 2859. They are early maturing varieties that take us out of hunger
I appreciate the nyanda groundnuts as well as the chi2 months sorghum varieties because they are early maturing seeds
Even if we have very low rainfalls, we are guaranteed that our crops will mature fully if we use new and improved varieties
MEN
TIED RIDGES
Men prefer tied ridges because they are quicker to do. They do not have to spend a lot of time in the field compared to the other methods
The men do not like the basin method because they say that it is painful. One spends a long time bending in the field digging the basins
A man would rather go and borrow cattle to do the tied ridges than to do dig basins which takes long and demands too much labor
LIVESTOCK MANAGEMENT
Men prefer to look after their cattle because they need to use them for farming
They also get manure, milk and meat from the cattle
They can easily sell their cattle so as to get money for seed and fertilizer
A man can run a business of ploughing for other people using his cattle, when the rainy season comes
Yes, they have equal opportunities. When farming meetings are called for, everyone is invited regardless of gender
We have the same opportunities to learn but when it comes to practically doing the work- the women do most of the work
We have the same chances but when the women have done all the work, the men want to take all the glory
We learn together but the men do not want to work. When the young men marry, they see their wives as slaves who must work for them

Yes we have situations where a woman has her own plot and a man has his. The truth though is that the woman is given the plot which has the worst type of soil by her husband to grow her crops. Though the other plots are referred to as the man’s- the truth is that they are household plots but controlled by the man and these plots are usually fertile or better than that one allocated to the woman.

[Do they consider proximity to the house?] In terms of proximity, the woman is given the plot which is furthest from the house. That is where she is allowed to dig her basins because men are lazy to walk to far away plots

[Are the other members of the family given their own plots to grow crops?] The children are not given their own plots. They are expected to help in the household plots. But if a young man marries he is given a plot by his father to grow his own crops and feed his family.

[What about size of the plot?] The woman is given the smallest plot to grow her groundnuts whist the man takes the largest plot because he says it is important to mainly focus on growing food for the family and crops to sell. She may be given just ¼ of an acre; some are given up to an acre.
A woman sometimes has to intercrop her maize with cow peas because she does not have enough land to grow the cow peas on their own plot

The men only come to their wives plots to plough with cattle. They do not do the rest of the chores unless the woman pleads with him to assist. The men would rather spend most of their time drinking beer than to help in the groundnuts plot.
Sometimes the men have to go and herd cattle therefore the women have to do most of the work in their own field.
The women always go to assist the men because the maize field belongs to the family. The women do most of the work though

Women will always go and work in their family maize and sorghum plots because they are commanded by their husbands to do so. A man can give his wife a command that she must work and finish with the family plots (clearing land, weeding and planting) before she can go and work in her plots failure to follow these commands can even result in the woman being assaulted by her husband.

A woman may brew beer or traditional drink and then invite people to come and assist her with work in her fields. After work the laborers are given beer or traditional drink and sadza to eat as payment.
She may hire extra labor that is always readily available around the villages and pay them in cash, maize or groundnuts

A woman’s farming responsibilities may be hindered if she has to fetch water from a borehole which is far from her place of residence

Going to the garden may also interfere with farming responsibilities
